entry.title: Anthropic and Nscale reportedly near a second $45B compute deal (2 minute read)
entry.content:
Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale are reportedly close to announcing a second $45 billion compute deal, just over a month after their first in August, though talks are ongoing and details could change. This would add to Anthropic's string of massive capacity commitments, even as some investors worry about spending outpacing profit. Nscale is also pursuing an IPO, but investors are pushing back on its proposed $30 billion valuation.

entry.title: Apple confirms Oct 28 event for its first touch-screen OLED MacBook Pro (2 minute read)
entry.content:
Apple confirmed an October 28 event in Los Angeles where it is expected to debut its first touch-screen Macs: 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros with tandem OLED panels, a Dynamic Island in place of the notch, a lighter build, and M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Apple is also expected to launch an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac on the M6, its first 2nm chip, in unchanged designs, plus an OLED iPad mini. Retail availability is expected November 6.

entry.title: SpacemiT Announces The V100 Server-Class RISC-V Processor (2 minute read)
entry.content:
SpacemiT claims its V100 chip is the first chip fully compliant with the RISC-V server specification. The chip packs 46 cores (6 XiangShan Kunminghu V2R2 plus 40 SpacemiT X100) at 2.2-2.4GHz on 12nm with a 120W TDP, supports eight-channel DDR5-4800 and 52 PCIe 5.0 lanes, and scales to two sockets and 92 cores. The specs trail Intel Xeon, AMD EPYC, and Arm server chips, and performance is untested.

entry.title: Nvidia Vera's memory system delivers 1.2 TB/s with flat latency, but cross-socket links lag (5 minute read)
entry.content:
Chips and Cheese's teardown of Vera's fabric found a 1024-bit LPDDR5X-9600 interface delivering 1.228 TB/s, with latency staying under 200 ns even as bandwidth load climbs, plus a 164 MB shared L3 and field-serviceable SOCAMM2 modules. NVLink C2C moves up to 780 GB/s between sockets, but cross-socket core-to-core latency is around 660 ns. Vera trails Graviton 5 on socket-level throughput but leads by nearly 20% in DRAM-bound SPEC tests.

entry.title: HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 Will Bring AI and HPC to the Moon on Astrolab FLIP (4 minute read)
entry.content:
HPE's Spaceborne Computer-4 will be the first HPC benchmark on the lunar surface, launching in late 2026 aboard Astrolab's FLIP rover under NASA's CLPS initiative. It will manage AI workloads such as vision inference and LiDAR data processing in the Moon's high-radiation, atmosphere-free environment. NASA and Deloitte are joining this mission to enhance AI capabilities, including Federated Learning and predictive cyber-analytics.

entry.title: SpaceX flies its Starfall return capsule for the second time on a 32-payload rideshare (3 minute read)
entry.content:
SpaceX launched its Starfall return capsule for the second time on the Bandwagon-5 rideshare, one of 32 payloads on a Falcon 9 booster flying for the 19th time. Per an FAA assessment, the disk-shaped capsule is about 10 feet wide and weighs 4,600 pounds, and can bring 2,200 pounds of payload home, aimed at microgravity research and in-space manufacturing. It deployed last, 2 hours 48 minutes after liftoff, alongside Varda's W-Series 7 capsule.

entry.title: Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer (13 minute read)
entry.content:
This article presents views from Synopsys, Keysight, Renesas, Arteris, Cadence, and Mixel on how physical AI changes chip design. Engineers must handle unpredictable environments, safety and serviceability, and split designs between devices that can rely on the cloud and those that must run fully locally, such as vehicles. Several speakers frame it as a sensing and imaging problem as much as a compute one.

entry.title: AI hardware design is the easy part, the lossy physical interface is the bottleneck (15 minute read)
entry.content:
AI will soon be superhuman at hardware design, but the digital-to-physical interface is lossy. Building real parts means navigating CNC/CAM translation, tolerance stacking, vendors, and scale, while measuring reality is sparse, slow, expensive, and sometimes qualitative. Demand is expected to shift toward suppliers of machined parts, harnesses, and components, plus better simulation and process-knowledge data.

entry.title: CXMT swings to a nearly $20B nine-month profit as AI demand drives up DRAM prices (2 minute read)
entry.content:
CXMT expects nine-month net profit of 131 to 132.5 billion yuan ($19.6 to $19.8 billion), versus a 5.3 billion yuan loss a year earlier, on revenue of 265 to 270 billion yuan, up from 32.1 billion. It credits AI-driven DRAM shortages, expanded capacity, and more output per wafer. Its claim of fifth-generation DRAM in mass production hasn't been independently verified, and memory booms typically fund new capacity that eventually pulls prices back down.

entry.title: NASA's Roman telescope beats its image-quality spec by nearly 30% after a hair-width mirror nudge (3 minute read)
entry.content:
After moving Roman's secondary mirror by about one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, engineers measured 63 nanometers RMS of optical error in the Wide Field Instrument, nearly 30% better than the 90-nanometer requirement. The camera has 18 detectors, and the same adjustment fixed slight defocus in the Coronagraph Instrument, which still needs testing of its ability to block unwanted light. Roman launched August 30, and both instruments now match or beat predictions.

entry.title: Tesla Roadster pairs underbody suction fans with cold-gas thrusters for grip beyond what tires allow (3 minute read)
entry.content:
The Roadster's floor uses fans and perimeter seals to pull air out from under the car, creating up to 2 g of suction, enough to hold it upside down while stationary, and at speed, front and rear passages open for more flow. Cold-gas thrusters add a second system: ten nozzles fed by compressed air, with all-electric actuators for fast micro-adjustments, which Tesla says push with four to five times the force tires can deliver.

entry.title: Variable frequency drives could free up grid power by cutting motor energy use 40 to 60 percent (5 minute read)
entry.content:
Variable frequency drives adjust motor speed to match demand, cutting a motor's energy use by about 40 to 60 percent. Toyota saved over $700,000 a year after putting them on 200-plus HVAC motors at its Kentucky plant, in a $1.25 million pilot. Cheaper sensors, machine-learning control, and power chips borrowed from EVs and solar inverters have cut costs. ABB claims drives on every motor could cover up to five years of data center load growth.

entry.title: Spin waves coupled to a superconducting circuit create a one-way street for microwave signals (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Argonne and UIUC researchers coupled spin waves in a thin yttrium iron garnet film to a superconducting resonator built directly on top, creating a hybrid mode that propagates one way and could keep return noise from leaking back into qubits. The key materials fix was swapping the usual rare-earth-containing substrate, which absorbs microwaves at low temperatures, for one without rare-earth metals. It's still a proof of concept.

entry.title: Kornia-SLAM: Visual-Inertial Odometry and SLAM in Rust (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Kornia-SLAM is an open-source visual-inertial odometry and spatial mapping library implemented entirely in Rust. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras coupled with inertial measurement units, utilizing factor graph optimization to maintain real-time performance and strict memory safety. This framework gives embedded software teams a reliable, crash-resilient foundation for real-time spatial estimation on compute-limited physical devices.

Featuring native spatio-temporal reasoning and low-latency action generation, it links high-level semantic understanding directly to robot execution through native bridges for ROS 2 and physics simulators like MuJoCo. The architecture allows creators of intelligent physical machines to translate natural language goals into dexterous, real-world manipulation and navigation.

entry.title: Google's Willow chip cuts quantum magic-state errors 40x with cultivation (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Google ran magic state cultivation on its Willow chip, cutting errors about 40x versus uncultivated states and reaching a record 99.99% logical fidelity for T-states. Magic states are a bottleneck because making them could consume up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity. Cultivation injects a noisy state into a small chip region, then uses coordinated measurements to discard flawed attempts, and Google grafted a distance-3 color code onto a distance-5 surface code. Larger-scale demonstrations are still needed.

Rocket Lab moved Neutron's debut to 2027 after finding voids in the carbon-composite layers of the forward dome on its first-stage propellant tank. It's the rocket's fourth slip since its 2021 unveiling, following a January tank rupture in testing, and shares fell about 10% after hours.

entry.title: Ayar Labs and GUC simulate a 3 kW co-packaged optics package, and only liquid cooling holds spec (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Ayar Labs and GUC simulated a 105mm by 140mm package with two XPUs, eight HBM4 stacks, and eight TeraPHY optical engines, offering over 100 Tbps of optical bandwidth at more than 3 kW. A standard air heatsink at 5 to 6 m/s failed spec, while an impingement liquid cold plate at 4.5 L/min kept the optical engines under 100°C. Results use static power assumptions, so dynamic workload simulation is next.

entry.title: Monazite ore could supply EV motor magnet metals, if the thorium waste can be handled (19 minute read)
entry.content:
Monazite ore is 45 to 70 percent rare earths by weight and carries all four elements motor magnets need (neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium), making it a leading path around China's roughly 90 percent market share. The catch is thorium, whose waste must be stored indefinitely. Energy Fuels already produces neodymium-praseodymium oxide plus pilot dysprosium and terbium at its Utah mill, while Saskatchewan's government-backed plant has produced little after six years and over CA$100 million.

entry.title: Building a GPU compiler from scratch, from PyTorch to CUDA (10 minute read)
entry.content:
This deep dive uses the Emmy compiler framework to follow PyTorch operations down to CUDA one lowering stage at a time: Tensor IR, Loop IR, Tile IR, Kernel IR, and finally emitted code. It uses RMSNorm and matrix multiplication as worked examples. It also covers operator fusion, schedule selection, and online attention rewrites, so readers can see what Triton-style stacks do under the hood.

entry.content:

By simulating factory layouts, automated optical inspection systems, and autonomous mobile robot fleets in virtual environments before physical deployment, the company minimizes factory commissioning delays and boosts production efficiency. This approach showcases how system architects and automation specialists can leverage high-fidelity simulation to safely validate and optimize complex robotic workcells prior to hardware installation.

entry.content:

Crews destacked the tower, added cryogenic propellant plumbing on the ground, and have begun restacking modules, while the launch bridge is restored. entry.title: Photonic chips learn after fabrication by measuring their own optical gradients (3 minute read)
entry.content:
A Nature Computational Science briefing describes an in situ learning method where photonic integrated circuits directly measure optical gradients, so diverse circuit layouts can be trained after they're built. That removes the need for a full digital model of the chip, which optical training normally leans on. The team demonstrated matrix design, multiwavelength computation, and rapid meta-learning on the hardware. Specifics like accuracy or energy figures aren't included.

entry.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM (2 minute read)
entry.content:
ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction from the Oxford Robot Dynamics Lab. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability

entry.title: Amazon builds its 1,000th Leo satellite at 27 a week, but only 396 are in orbit (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Amazon built its 1,000th Leo broadband satellite at its Kirkland, Washington plant, which took six months to produce its first 27 and now turns out 27 a week. It builds propulsion in-house and borrowed consumer electronics methods to cut tests that took weeks down to hours. The bottleneck is launch: only 396 are in orbit against 3,232 needed, and the Vulcan grounding and a New Glenn pad explosion cost Amazon FCC spectrum priority.

entry.title: Google open-sources ML Drift, a GPU engine that runs one shader set across OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and OpenGL ES (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Tensor virtualization decouples a tensor's logical layout from its physical GPU allocation, so one shader template replaces separate backend-specific codebases. For edge LLMs, ML Drift switches kernels between compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode, using a convolution-aligned KV cache layout and in-kernel activation quantization to skip memory roundtrips. It cut YouTube Shorts frame latency by up to 40%, and Google co-optimized it with Arm, Intel, and Qualcomm GPUs.

entry.title: Supercapacitor cement is key to buildings that store their own power (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Scientists from the Harbin Institute of Technology developed a cement-based supercapacitor capable of powering small devices like LEDs. The device uses a 3D-printed electrode ink made from carbon nanotubes and cement, enabling fast energy discharge. Future research will enhance cold-weather performance, potentially allowing buildings to store energy and support smart environments.

entry.title: Too many quantum startups, too little money to keep them alive (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Gartner predicts that over half of quantum startups will fail by 2030 due to a market unable to generate sufficient revenue. Despite this, companies are investing in quantum technologies for their potential business advantages, focusing on building expertise rather than waiting for technological maturity. The public sector and financial industries are expected to lead quantum computing investments, with spending reaching $245 million and $289 million by 2027 and 2028, respectively.
